subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this custom cooperative glob walker and bootstrap-hook scheduling as the bounded fix despite possible prompt-ordering and session-timing changes for existing extra-bootstrap configurations?
rationale: The implementation and proof are strong, but bootstrap matching and context construction are compatibility-sensitive session surfaces where automation cannot safely choose the upgrade tradeoff.

options.title: Land After Refresh
options.body: Accept the focused implementation, refresh it onto current main, and merge after exact-head checks and focused bootstrap tests pass.

options.title: Require Live Channel Proof
options.body: Keep the implementation but require one current-head embedded-run or channel-latency transcript showing channel I/O remains responsive during bootstrap.

options.title: Pause For Broader Design
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers prefer worker isolation, priority scheduling, or caching instead of owning a custom glob implementation.

recommendation.title: Land After Refresh
recommendation.body: Accept the focused implementation, refresh it onto current main, and merge after exact-head checks and focused bootstrap tests pass.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history spans the internal hooks, bootstrap hooks, and guarded workspace-read boundaries central to this decision.
